reviews.title: Predatory and not helpful
reviews.text: I downloaded this and did the free trial. It was cumbersome to use and the format to set up was confusing that had me doing tasks that were intended to be daily, multiple times a day. I tried to cancel before I was charged by going in the settings in the app but could not find anywhere to discontinue the trial. I deleted my account and the app and a few days later I was charged for the full year subscription. It feels like this app is taking advantage of people with ADHD by advertising this app is for them, knowing full well tasks like cancelling subscriptions are hard for them to complete and then making it extremely difficult to do so. Do not download unless you want to flush $54 down the toilet.

reviews.title: Asking TOO SOON
reviews.text: Maybe I’ll change this. Ive literally it on this app for four minutes and then asked twice to review it. This means what do I think about it ? I like it do I not like it ? Would I recommend it to other people ? It’s so ridiculous to ask me so soon. It’s what most apps do. It’s very disappointing for one that’s supposed to be intelligent. I skipped the first ask you know I was annoyed . But then it popped up again . So for now one star- for being too needy, like all the other apps- because that’s the only thing I really know for sure after four minutes.

reviews.title: Still needs tons of improvement on desktop
reviews.text:
I really love this app on mobile, but on desktop it’s much harder to do what I do on my phone.

I can’t delete lists on the desktop app, and the emojis glitch in the calendar day view, so it’s hard to see which part of the day you’re in.

I use this app a lot in both my personal and professional life because it makes it easy to see how the day is going and to move activities around. For work, though, it’s not ideal, because the Mac app is much weaker than the iPhone one. Because of that, I have to use the browser, and I can’t keep my work activities up to date easily. My job requires me to have hundreds of tabs open, so I lose track of the app’s tab and of what I need to do. Some days I end up going back to a notepad to remember my tasks, which defeats the main purpose of the app: helping people with ADHD.

Technically, on Mac it’s just one more app for listing tasks, not one that actually helps with ADHD.

reviews.title: What happened to the confetti???
reviews.text:
Update: one of the things I liked most about this app was the little celebratory confetti effect when I marked a task completed. It was an acknowledgment of effort and helped me stay motivated to keep working towards completing my tasks. Now it’s gone and Tiimo has gone from being genuinely useful to me, and being recommended to others by me, to something utilitarian that can easily be replaced with Apple’s built in reminders App. I’m very disappointed.

I’ve found this app to be helpful in keeping me focused on the things I want to accomplish. I know that it has more capability than I utilize, but I simply don’t need all of it. I do have one complaint and that’s with the frequent push for users to upgrade to premium. I’ve gotten pop ups every time I open the app this week encouraging me to take advantage of a premium subscription discount. It’s very frustrating to have my concentration disrupted by a sales pitch before I’m allowed to add a task. Now, with this most recent update, the option to choose an emoji symbol relevant to my task has been moved behind the premium pay wall. 

I understand that the developers are in business to turn a profit, but the tactic of gradually eliminating functionality feels disingenuous. If it continues, free account users will either feel forced to pay, or give up on the app altogether. I sincerely hope it won’t come to that for me.

reviews.title: Quick review
reviews.text: During onboarding this app asks for a review, before I’ve gotten any value out of it at all, so here’s your review: you force me into a week trial to try it for free that will charge me over $50 bucks if I forget, or I’d have to pay $14 for one month with no free trial. So I’ll cancel as soon as I finish onboarding so I get the trial and don’t have to worry about forgetting. Then you ask for this review before I’ve used it for even 5 minutes, when all you’ve done so far is cost me time and effort. The predatory trial is a dark pattern that hopes users will forget to cancel. So you get 1 star, I would give 0 if I could. You’re welcome.

reviews.title: Trust a real review this app sux
reviews.text: These people giving glowing reviews must be friends of the maker and/or paid.  This is just another to do list. It is not intuitive at all, and it is extremely difficult to figure out how to do even basic things.  Creating barriers is not how you get a chronic procrastinator on board. Do they know ADHD people at all? Also the pay version adds nothing. Don’t waste your money!  The AI is not helpful at all.  It just makes a to do list for you- like I could do that!  The problem is I have a to do list 9 pages long and I don’t know where to begin, what are the priorities- what can be back-burnered.  So I do nothing or I do what’s easy or I hyper-focus on something that could wait while something else is on fire.  I have dozens of apps on my phone that can remind me to do stuff, but building habits takes more than that.  If you need another to-do list, go for it but don’t think this is some kind of game-changing magic bullet because it’s not.

reviews.title: App took a step backwards with AI
reviews.text: The docs and screenshots throughout how to articles suggest that you can make templates for activities.l and reuse these.  You cannot, they gutted the app and instead you have to now completely setup your tasks exactly how you want to use it all in one go.  No personal templates.  Additionally you are pressured to go through ai prompts to try and do thjngs.  The AI duplicates tasks, if it creates anything at all, feels very detached and not a great experience.  It’s worse than talking to a neurotypical on many levels including miscommunication and misunderstandings. Ai for the sake of ai is gross. Spend more time using it internally before releasing it at least.  Feels like they gutted the app functionality in favor of AI. The desktop webapp honestly shouldn’t exist as it is only the calendar piece of the app, and an extremely poor version of that feature at that, no access to templates at all and weirdly has more display options than the mobile app.  It has some good templates prebuilt in the app of course but forget making your own to show up in the template browser.  Wouldn’t surprise me if that goes away and you are forced to talk or type to ai to do anything soon.   Very disappointed that it’s not as described in their own faq and how to docs. The ios 27 feature list confirms thats where this is headed

reviews.title: Lots of wasted potential
reviews.text: I use AI to do my job, so the idea of this app as a light personal assistant seemed like a very useful application of the tech. In practice, this chat bot is really dumb and cannot actually parse a slightly nuanced todo or deal with a big brain dump. You also can only accept or reject its actions, you can’t correct them to tell the LLM what was wrong when the only issue is the time or a misheard word. For example, I said I needed to pick something up on the way home from an appointment, so it scheduled that reminder for 90min after the appointment ended instead of at the end time, but that was so many taps to correct it wasn’t really worth using the AI to begin with. It is not remotely capable of transforming a nebulous description of chores into actionable, scheduled steps, despite basically putting that ability on the tin. It’s really just a purpose built Siri focused only on reminders, and it can do a whole lot less than Siri. Add to that the UI is just plain confusing and unintuitive, things are divided into tabs in the most useless way, and none of the top level tabs feel as useful as they should be. This app feels like work to use when it’s supposed to make things easier.

reviews.title: NOT for ADHD brain, wasted so much time trying to set up
reviews.text: Not good for this ADHD brain! I wanted to use this to schedule tasks and keep from getting sidetracked, but instead I’m practically in tears after wasting over an hour trying to set up my schedule. I used the AI “Co-Planner” and spoke out what I need to get done today, and it did add everything to my task list but didn’t suggest specific time slots as I had expected. I tried using the Co-Planner to edit and add time slots to all of the tasks (plan my day for me, as I thought this app was supposed to do), but it says I don’t have anything planned! I asked it to change the time of a scheduled task and it asks for the title of the task, then says it can’t find the task! The only way to change anything is to manually go into each task and update the time/duration, which I already have the option to do on my calendar app FOR FREE! The AI feature is also super slow on both PC and iPhone, and it stopped responding completely when I tried using it on my phone. Visually, I can see it being useful IF and ONLY IF it were easier to set up a schedule in the first place. I’m really disappointed in all of the ADHD/AuDHD influencers out there who have recommended this app and I feel like the good reviews have to be phony. I can’t see how anyone with a neurodivergent brain could honestly say this app helped them, unless they have someone else doing the setup and scheduling. Now I’ve wasted even more time writing this review so others with a brain like mine don’t suffer the same fate!

reviews.title: Buggy and unhelpful AI
reviews.text: First day and this was so frustrating. The ai could not complete making the requested task. When it finally created it after 20 minutes of begging it told me there’s no way to make it show in the Ui that it’s a task for every 6 months but to rest assured that it’s that way in the backend . That’s not good enough for me. I need it to show me in the UI accurate details. The superscript is only for the general to do list not for daily tasks but my to do list is weekly and I don’t want to see that number all the time. I’d rather something I can easily reduce like with daily tasks or have the option to choose what the superscript shows. The ai randomly started speaking in Dutch and repeating stuff . Really poor ai I work with Ai daily and this is one of the buggiest I’ve seen. For the timed tasks I can’t click a button to extend the task it just moves to the next thing. There should be an option to say I’m done. There’s no way to disable the lofi from automatically playing. I’m autistic I don’t want sound in my ears. It doesn’t help me and comes on when I move to that page no matter how often I close it and you should give options to remove it fully from the page. Definitely no autoplay. Glad you had a free trial. This would be nice if you’d give more customization.
